verdict_text: NO. The cast regex omits `self_attn.o_proj.weight`, matching only 6 projection matrices per layer instead of 7, so it casts 96 tensors to bfloat16 and leaves the 16 `o_proj` weights in float32 — violating Required result clause 1 ("cast exactly the 112 projection matrices ... to bfloat16", where the list includes `o_proj`). The required checks are correspondingly weakened rather than enforced: the count assert hardcodes `is: 96` and the comment redefines the check as "exactly 96 tensors are bfloat16", so the plan will not fail loudly on the missing 16 casts as the "exactly 112 tensors are bfloat16" check demands. The negative-lookahead float32 assert compounds this by actively asserting that `o_proj` is float32, cementing the wrong dtype. The remaining parts (no deletions, unchanged names, 114-tensor count, `out/T3` with 256 MiB sharding) are consistent with the spec, but the dtype result is wrong and grading is bit-exact on dtypes.
expected_defect: One projection family is missing from the bfloat16 cast pattern (the attention output projection stays float32); the artifact's own count check was adjusted to the wrong number.
